'''''Quercus estremadurensis''''' is a [[species]] of [[oak]] in the family [[Fagaceae]], [[Native species|native]] to [[Portugal]], western [[Spain]] and [[Morocco]].<ref name=POWO_359617-1/> It was first described by [[Otto Karl Anton Schwarz]] in 1935.<ref name=IPNI_359617-1/> It has also been treated as a subspecies of ''[[Quercus robur]]'', ''Q. robur'' subsp. ''estremadurensis''.<ref name=POWO_359617-1/> It is placed in [[Quercus sect. Quercus|section ''Quercus'']].<ref name="Denk17App21" />

==Description==
''Quercus estremadurensis'' is a mostly deciduous tree (when mature rarely marcescent or semievergreen) within the roburoid<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Schwarz |first=O. |date=1936 |title=Einige neue Eichen des Mediterrangebiets und Vorderasiens |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/3994908 |journal=Notizblatt des Königl. Botanischen Gartens und Museums zu Berlin |volume=116 |issue=BD XIII |pages=1–22 |doi=10.2307/3994908 |jstor=3994908|url-access=subscription }}</ref> quercus subsection (that also comprises ''[[Quercus robur]]'', ''[[Quercus petraea]]'', ''[[Quercus hartwissiana]]'' and ''[[Quercus canariensis]]'') thus sharing a good number of features with its closest relative ''[[Quercus robur]]'' such as bearing shortly petiolate broad and glabrous auriculated leaves, and long peduncled acorns. Also features close resemblance to other members of that subsection as happens with young tomentose sprouts and branches and fairly well elongated leaves brandishing high number of shallow lobes such as we can find in ''[[Quercus canariensis]]'' or ''[[Quercus hartwissiana]]''.

Due to its relictic status of conservation and its high propension to hybridise with any other surrounding quercus species, many characteristics are still certainly not easy to clear cut and lie under deep scientific discussion.

==Distribution==
Cited only in a few loci scatterly placed all over the southwestern district of the Iberian peninsula where the species might have survived the increasing process of aridification that took place in the mediterranean basin after the slow retreat of glacial conditions during last glaciation<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vazquez Pardo |first=Francisco Maria |date=September 20, 2009 |title=Estatus de conservación de Quercus robur susbp. estremadurensis (O.Schwarz) A.Camus en Extremadura (España). |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/235930381  |website=researchgate.net}}</ref> and suffering the effects of a [[Bottleneck effect|bottleneck]] phenomenon that clearly did not allow the populations to counteract and recover lost environments. Thus the cited locations for the species only contain one to five individuals but the occurrence is nevertheless not to be overlooked, occurring from Ourense in southern Galicia to northern Morocco in no less than one hundred stands, most of them appearing in the central part of Portugal both near the coast and in the mountainous interior. Over the border with Spain it has been found in Extremadura and west Andalusia, with its easternmost stand in the mountain range of [[Siruela]], Badajoz.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Romero Mohedano |first=Rafael |date=2014 |title=Presencia del Roble Pedunculado (Quercus robur L., Fagaceae) en la Sierra de Siruela (Badajoz, España) |url=https://dialnet.unirioja.es/servlet/articulo?codigo=6422062 |website=Dialnet|issue=8 |pages=45–54 }}</ref>
